tips.text: Taeguk refers to the source of everything in the universe and the universal law in which
everything continuously goes through cycles of creation and destruction.
Taeguk paljang stands for gom and symbolizes the source of growth.
Taeguk paljang is also a pumsae that summarizes the basics and represents mature techniques
of Taekwondo when moving on from an initiate to becoming a belt holder.
We will now take a look at the pumsae of Taeguk paljang.
Taeguk paljang consists of six key moves, namely dubal dangseongjagi, kkoduro bakkadmakgi,
waesan dulmakgi, dangyeo jirugi, kkoduro aramakgi, and ddiyeo apjagi.
These are the six key moves of Taeguk paljang.
We will now take a closer look at each of the key moves of Taeguk paljang.
Dubal dangseongjagi is a kicking technique where you jump and perform two midair
kicks in succession.
The first balchagi lightly kicks the target at the torso level, and the second balchagi
kicks a target higher with the other foot.
Koduro bakkadmakgi is a technique to block with your hands with help from the assisting hand.

Weesan dulmakgi is a technique where your arms are crossed in front of your chest.
The inner arm blocks the lower body, and the outer arm performs olgul anpalmok bakkadmakgi.

Tangyo jirugi is a technique used mostly to strike the chin by pulling an opponent's clothing.
The jirugi starts at the chest line with the fist pulled back.
The fist performing jirugi passes by the wrist being pulled back and reaches the target.
Be careful not to let the hammer fist touch the front of the shoulder performing jirugi.
Also, be careful not to let the fist start at the back and perform jirugi upward, like chichirugi.
